sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Bibliography only. Gaikundi index: Ambuwat & Nate 1976 (Dictionaries of PNG 3, Gaikundi-Pidgin, SIL, 44 pp.), Nate 1975, Saun & Nate 1976, 1976, 1978 (scripture); 'Gaikunti (see Gaikundi) Schanely n.d.'; SCHANELY, Leon E. (SIL): 'n.d. Phonemic statement of Gaikunti (d. of Sawos). TS. (ment'd Laycock, PL B-25, 28)'. No other descriptive work on Gaikundi listed.

sources.citation: Staalsen, Philip. 1966. The phonemes of Iatmul. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 5, Pacific Linguistics A-7: 69-76.
sources.note: Describes Iatmul (Nyaura), not Gaikundi: 'Stress is sometimes related to and predictable by the vowel' / no contrastive stress (p. 74). Context for the nearest relative only; not a Gaikundi statement.

sources.citation: Aikhenvald, Alexandra Y. 2008. The Manambu language of East Sepik, Papua New Guinea. Oxford: OUP. Ch. 1, note 3.
sources.note: Nothing on Gaikundi stress. Identity: '(Burui, Maligwat, and Gaikundi, listed as separate Ndu languages on the Ethnologue website, are among the Iatmul dialects.)... Sengo, Burui, Kwaruwi Kundi, and also Gaikundi appear to be members of the Iatmul continuum... A reliable reappraisal of the languages covered by "Sawos" is in Staalsen (1975).'

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. (ed.). TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Gaikundi' (154 lexical items; source: Summer Institute of Linguistics Language Survey of Gaikundi, 1991).
sources.note: Wordlist only; four of the 50 saved forms carry a stress mark ('buni 'back', 'lapu 'banana', 'yuwi 'feather', ipmáŋgu 'cold'); no prose statement about stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1991. Three vowels, semivowels, and neutralisation: orthographic and other problems of Sepik languages. Pacific Linguistics A-73: 107ff.
sources.note: No mention of Gaikundi, Sawos, or stress.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Entry 91 SAWOS (Gaikunti, Kwongai, Sepik Plains, Tshuosh, Tshwosh), pp. 27-28: 'An SIL worker, L. Schanely, has prepared an unpublished phonemic statement of one Sawos dialect which he calls Gaikunti ("village-language").'

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1965. The Ndu language family (Sepik District, New Guinea). Pacific Linguistics C-1. Canberra: ANU. xi+224 pp.
sources.note: Gaikundi/Gaikunti never named. Ch. 14 'Notes on the Sawos language' p. 144: 'it was not possible to elicit material in Sawos'. The stress section 5.2 (pp. 29-30) is for Wosera Abelam only (non-phonemic, nucleus-rank rule). No Gaikundi stress statement.
Nothing on stress; classification refs Aikhenvald 2015, Laycock 1965; comment Staalsen 1975: 11; alternative names Gaikunti, Gaikwundi, Sawos.
No phonology or stress information; cites Ethnologue 18 only.

sources.citation: Jendraschek, Gerd. 2012. A grammar of Iatmul. Habilitationsschrift, Universitaet Regensburg. xv+564 pp. (stress pp. 91-93).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: If Aikhenvald 2008 is right that Gaikundi belongs to the Iatmul dialect continuum, the Iatmul stress rule (long vowels > CVC > initial syllable, per the Wikipedia summary) is the nearest description and its village list may place Gaikundi.

sources.citation: Summer Institute of Linguistics. 1991. Language survey of Gaikundi (SIL PNG survey wordlist; source of the ASJP GAIKUNDI and TransNewGuinea.org lists).

sources.note: The original survey sheet behind the stress-marked wordlist forms on TransNewGuinea.org; survey wordlists sometimes carry a one-line note on stress placement.
